This is another one of those things I see all over various social media groups … Boozy Desserts. These are treats you won’t see in your local grocery store cases.

They seem to be popping up more and more everywhere lately, mostly with home bakers. You can get the alcohol in the batter (which cooks off but leaves flavor), the alcohol mixed into the frosting (making it essentially alcoholic frosting as nothing cooks off) or you can get the alcohol put into pipettes which basically gives you a mini shot of alcohol with different volumes – depending on what pipettes you use.

Alcohol in fruit and baked goods can be a slippery slope though and people don’t understand you can in fact get in trouble for it – liquor license, if you don’t have one, don’t sell boozy goods. If you have a good cake artist they should be well-educated on the issue as no one wants to get into trouble, be fined or face possible jail time in certain places!

From looking around the internet, selling goods where the alcohol in the batter is fine, as the alcohol content bakes off while in the oven. You can put alcohol in the frosting as long as it is 10% or less of the frosting ingredients (this varies from state to state though, so research!).

For me personally, selling goods with alcohol filled pipettes in them is crossing a line – at that point I would not feel comfortable. However to get around this, I would add the pipette cost to an order, supply the pipettes and the client can purchase the alcohol, fill them and add them to the goods themselves.
